subject: MAP: token economics & orchestration checks for Novaware POC
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Alex Simmons <alex.simmons@novaware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: token economics & orchestration checks for Novaware POC

Alex — thanks for the call today. Per our agreement, I'm drafting a compact MAP subsection that focuses on the cost/unit-econ checks we need to clear before POC close. I attached a short traffic sample and a first-pass MAP doc (map-draft-v1.pdf).

High-level asks from Redwood to validate viability and set gating criteria:
- Representative traffic profile (per-minute QPS, session lengths, user concurrency) — earliest needed by Wed 5/7.
- Privacy constraints for caching (can we persist prefixes or only stateless hashing?).
- Target p95 latency SLA (and whether 200ms p95 is required for all routes).
- Acceptance thresholds for token cost: target tokens/$ or max $/MAU you expect for POC.

Immediate Redwood assumptions we plan to validate in the MAP (please review):
1) Avg input prompt: 120 tokens, avg generation: 220 tokens (client-provided sample shows this distribution).
2) KV prefix caching eligible for ~30–50% of requests (non-PII), TTL default 6h for POC unless you require longer.
3) Microbatching target: 8–12 requests per batch during normal load; burst batching up to 32 for short spikes.
4) Cost envelopes: using q4-quantized model variant we estimate 2.6M tokens == $1 baseline; we will run sims for other quantization/replica configurations.

Next steps / timeline we propose for MAP close:
- Tue 5/6: Redwood runs burst/microbatch sim with your traffic sample and returns a short summary (tokens/$ at three operating points).
- Wed 5/7: Joint review call to agree gating thresholds (cache hit rate, batch size floor, p95 latency target).
- Fri 5/9: Sign-off on MAP subsection and go/no-go for dedicated capacity POC.

If any of the assumptions above are off, flag them and we'll re-run sims.

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: novaware_traffic_sample.csv, map-draft-v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Simmons <alex.simmons@novaware.com>
Date: Mon, 05 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: token economics & orchestration checks for Novaware POC

Michael / Alex — quick technical pass on the assumptions and proposed gating. I ran a lightweight tabletop with the attached sample (see linked internal sheet) and here are pragmatic numbers we should use in the MAP to avoid surprises: 

Assumptions we validated quickly:
- Avg prompt 120 tokens / avg response 220 tokens (matches sample).
- Session composition: ~65% short lookups (<100 tokens), 25% medium (100–400 tokens), 10% long (>400 tokens).

Suggested MAP gating thresholds (conservative):
- Cache eligibility: assume 35% hit rate for POC (we can model 50% as optimistic). Novaware constraint: if PII blocks caching, treat 35% as upper bound.
- Default batch size for simulations: 10 requests/batch at steady state, microbatching window 20ms. For burst windows (10–30s) allow batching to 24–32 to improve token efficiency but classify as 'degraded latency-friendly' mode.
- Latency impact: batching baseline adds ~12–25ms per-token overhead for queued requests; at batch size 10 expect +18ms median, +55ms 95th if queueing at peak without autoscale.

Cost modeling (quick estimates) — per 1M output tokens: 
- q4_0 quant (our low-precision): $0.38 per 1k output tokens -> ~$380 per 1M output tokens.
- q8_1 variant (higher quality): ~$620 per 1M output tokens.
- These vary with KV cache hit-rate and batching: each 10% additional cache hit reduces token billing ~8–10% (prefetch + prefix caching avoids repeated prompt tokens).

Operational suggestions for MAP: 
- Add a conservative 'burst cost cap' step in the MAP: if daily cost projection > 2x baseline for >2 consecutive days, trigger throttling/fallback to smaller model.
- Track tokens-per-session and tokens-per-user daily in Redwood Console dashboard we provision for you (we'll include a sample token burn report).

Links: internal sim sheet (https://drive.google.com/sheet/sim-novaware), internal run id HBSP-23456.

I'll run a microbatch sim against two operating points tonight and attach quick sim stub for Irene to convert into a formal MAP appendix.

Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure & Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: sim-stub-results.csv (placeholder), link to internal sheet
From: Alex Simmons <alex.simmons@novaware.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 May 2025 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: token economics & orchestration checks for Novaware POC

Thanks Michael — good structure. Quick answers from our side so you can run the sims against realistic constraints: 

Traffic profile (approx):
- Monthly active users (MAU): 2,100 during POC window.
- Typical concurrency: baseline 12–25 QPS, peak windows up to 150 QPS for 2–3 minute bursts (~10% of days).
- Session behaviour: ~18 interactions per session on average, but many are single-turn lookups.

Content & caching constraints:
- We cannot persist any string that contains user PII. That means we can cache on hashed prefixes where PII is removed. In practice this will cut eligibility; please model a conservative TTL 24h but assume effective hit-rate closer to 25–35% unless pre-processing is applied.

Latency SLA:
- Target p95: 200ms for the primary summarization route. If caching increases p95 beyond that, we'll need a fallback/priority queue for interactive users.

Budget guidance:
- For the POC we have an internal target of <$4k total model spend for the month (exclusive of Redwood platform fees). If that is infeasible at your conservative thresholds, flag the shortfall and recommend mitigations (smaller model, stronger caching, or stricter throttles).

We can push a sanitized 48-hour trace if that would help your sims — I can get that to you by EOD.

— Alex
Alex Simmons
Head of Product, Novaware
ops@novaware.com
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 May 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: token economics & orchestration checks for Novaware POC

Looping back — Ben's tabletop results look reasonable. I'll run two short microbatch simulations with their sanitized 24h trace once we have it (Ben: use the conservative cache hit-rate 25% and the optimistic 45% case). Deliverables and timing: 
- Thu 5/8 EOD: sim summary (tokens/$ at steady, peak-burst, and degraded-batch modes) + run artifacts attached (sim-results-stub.json attached here as placeholder).
- Fri 5/9: MAP appendix draft with gating rows (cache hit %, batch size, predicted p95) for the sign-off meeting.

Notes on simulation knobs we'll exercise:
- model variants (q4_0, q8_1)
- batching window: 0ms (no batching), 20ms microbatch, 100ms burst-window
- cache TTL: none, 6h, 24h (and a hashed-prefix-only policy)

If Novaware sends the sanitized trace, we'll run the sims against both the default MAP timeline and a worst-case traffic stress to see where the $4k budget lands.

Irene
Irene Choi
Applied ML — Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sim-results-stub.json
